_comment: Connect tab tools (docs/IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md Phase 2b step 1). Placeholders: {{baseURL}} (no /v1), {{apiKey}}, {{model}}, {{host}}, {{port}}. Verified against each tool's docs on 2026-09-23 — re-check docsURL when editing. minContext (optional): the smallest model context the tool works with — Claude Code's first request measured 15,114 tokens, Codex's about 7,000; Cline/Roo per their docs. launch (optional): how `quail launch <id|alias>` starts the tool pointed at Quail — command, args, env, and files written to a temp dir ({{tempDir}}); never the user's own config files.

integrations.name: Claude Code
integrations.where: Your shell (before running `claude`), or the "env" block of ~/.claude/settings.json
integrations.notes: Best-effort: Anthropic doesn't support Claude Code with non-Claude models, so tool use depends on the model. The base URL has no /v1 — Claude Code adds /v1/messages itself. Every model variable points at this model because Claude Code also asks for separate background and sub-agent models, which the server would reject. Needs a large context; Quail sets it per model from this Mac's memory. Don't put this in a project's committed .claude/settings.json.

integrations.name: OpenAI Codex CLI
integrations.snippet:
model = "{{model}}"
model_provider = "quail"

[model_providers.quail]
name = "Quail (llama.cpp)"
base_url = "{{baseURL}}/v1"
env_key = "QUAIL_API_KEY"
wire_api = "responses"

# and in your shell:
# export QUAIL_API_KEY={{apiKey}}
integrations.notes: Codex only speaks the Responses API now; llama.cpp serves /v1/responses, but agent-loop support (tools, reasoning items) is newer than its chat API. The provider id can't be openai, ollama or lmstudio. Add model_context_window = <tokens> so compaction works for a model Codex doesn't know.

integrations.name: Continue
integrations.snippet:
name: Quail
version: 0.0.1
schema: v1

models:
  - name: {{model}} (Quail)
    provider: openai
    model: {{model}}
    apiBase: {{baseURL}}/v1
    apiKey: {{apiKey}}
    roles:
      - chat
      - edit
      - apply
integrations.notes: With provider: openai the apiBase includes /v1. Add a second model with the autocomplete role if you want tab completions.

integrations.name: Cline
integrations.where: Cline settings (gear icon) → API Provider: OpenAI Compatible
integrations.notes: Set up in Cline's own settings screen, not a file. Under Model Configuration, set Context Window to the model's context so Cline's large prompts fit.

integrations.name: Roo Code
integrations.where: Roo Code settings (gear icon) → Providers → API Provider: OpenAI Compatible
integrations.notes: Roo Code relies on native tool calling, so pick a model that handles tools well. Set the context window under Model Configuration.

integrations.name: Zed
integrations.where: Zed settings.json (zed: open settings); the API key in the Agent panel's settings for "quail"
integrations.notes: Zed keeps keys out of settings.json: enter {{apiKey}} in the Agent panel's provider settings, or launch Zed with QUAIL_API_KEY set. max_tokens is the context window — match the model's.

integrations.name: aider
integrations.notes: The openai/ prefix on the model is required. aider warns about an unknown model's context size; --no-show-model-warnings silences it.

integrations.name: opencode
integrations.notes: If your global opencode config sets a default model, it wins over this file's "model" — pick Quail's with /models in the TUI, or opencode run -m quail/{{model}}. List every model you want under models; limit.context drives compaction. Known issue under investigation: in one test opencode reported "Cannot connect to API" against Quail's endpoint even though other clients reached it — if you hit this, please report it.

integrations.name: Goose
integrations.notes: OPENAI_HOST has no /v1 — Goose adds v1/chat/completions itself.

integrations.name: Open WebUI
integrations.where: Admin Settings → Connections → OpenAI API → Add Connection
integrations.snippet:
URL: {{baseURL}}/v1
API Key: {{apiKey}}
Model IDs: leave empty (it reads /v1/models)

# Running Open WebUI in Docker? Use this URL instead:
# http://host.docker.internal:{{port}}/v1
integrations.notes: Set it in the Admin UI: Open WebUI's OPENAI_API_* environment variables only apply on first launch. Choosing llama.cpp as the connection's provider adds model loading controls.

integrations.name: LibreChat
integrations.where: librechat.yaml in the LibreChat folder, plus QUAIL_API_KEY in .env
integrations.snippet:
version: 1.3.15
endpoints:
  custom:
    - name: 'Quail'
      apiKey: '${QUAIL_API_KEY}'
      baseURL: '{{baseURL}}/v1'
      models:
        default: ['{{model}}']
        fetch: true
      titleConvo: true
      modelDisplayLabel: 'Quail'

# .env:
# QUAIL_API_KEY={{apiKey}}
integrations.notes: In Docker, use http://host.docker.internal:{{port}}/v1 as the baseURL. fetch: true lists every model the server has.

integrations.name: curl
integrations.notes: Add "stream": true for streamed output. {{baseURL}}/health needs no key — a quick first check.

integrations.name: Python
integrations.snippet:
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(
    base_url="{{baseURL}}/v1",
    api_key="{{apiKey}}",
)

completion = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="{{model}}",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Hello!"}],
)
print(completion.choices[0].message.content)
integrations.notes: The SDK insists on a non-empty api_key even when the server has none.

integrations.name: JavaScript / TypeScript
integrations.notes: apiKey must be non-empty even when the server has none.
